chunks: "I'd draw the output characteristics: drain current on the y-axis, drain-source voltage on the x-axis, and a family of curves, one for each gate-source voltage.
For V GS below threshold, the curve sits on the x-axis: no channel, no current. Above threshold, each curve starts at the origin and rises roughly linearly at first.
That's the triode region, where the MOSFET acts like a resistor whose value is set by V GS , so a higher V GS gives a steeper line.
As V DS increases, the curve bends over and flattens. That's saturation, where the current is set by V GS and barely depends on V DS : I D equals 1 over 2 k n(V GS-V t) squared .
I'd draw a dashed parabola through the knees of the curves. That's the boundary V DS equals V GS minus V t . Left of it is triode, right of it is saturation.
Two details I'd point out. Because current is square-law in overdrive, equal steps in V GS give increasingly spaced curves.
And in a real device the saturation curves tilt up slightly because of channel-length modulation.
If they want the transfer curve too, I'd draw I D versus V GS : zero until V t , then a parabola rising."
